Matching the seizure syndrome

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 7-year-old girl has frequent brief staring episodes with immediate recovery and no history of convulsive seizures. Hyperventilation provokes an episode, and EEG shows generalized 3-Hz spike-and-wave activity. Which medication specifically targets this seizure syndrome?

  1. Carbamazepine
  2. Gabapentin
  3. Phenylephrine
  4. Ethosuximide
  5. Phenytoin
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Ethosuximide

The presentation is typical absence epilepsy, for which ethosuximide is an established treatment.

Understanding the options

Ethosuximide
The presentation is typical absence epilepsy, for which ethosuximide is an established treatment.
Phenytoin
Phenytoin is not an appropriate treatment for typical absence seizures.
Carbamazepine
Carbamazepine may aggravate absence seizures.
Gabapentin
Gabapentin is not a standard treatment for this generalized absence syndrome.
Phenylephrine
This adrenergic agonist is not an antiseizure treatment.
